body.en: Circles bring their own angle and length rules: the relationship between central and inscribed angles, the right angle in a semicircle, and arcs and sectors as fractions of the whole.

Circumference \( C=2\pi r \); area \( A=\pi r^{2} \). The inscribed angle is half the central angle on the same arc, so the angle in a semicircle is \( 90^{\circ} \). An arc and sector scale by \( \dfrac{\theta}{360} \).

Euclidean Invariants, Locus Equations & Scaling Laws: In analytic geometry, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A circle of center \((h, k)\) and radius \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a tangent line at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the radius \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).

A \(90^\circ\) central sector represents exactly \(1 / 4\) of the total circle area: Area = \((90/360) \cdot \pi (4)^{2} = 4\pi \approx 12.57\).

Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central Angle & Circle Completion Works: Given \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the radius is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any circle, drawing diameter \(POQ\) splits an inscribed angle \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior angle theorem, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).

A triangle is inscribed in a circle with one side as the diameter. Find the angle opposite that side.

The angle in a semicircle is a right angle:

\[ 90^{\circ}. \]

Find the area of a \( 90^{\circ} \) sector of a circle with \( r=4 \). Take \( \pi=3.14 \).

\[ \frac{90}{360}\,\pi r^{2}=\tfrac14\times 3.14\times 16=12.56. \]

label.en: Common Pitfall — Inscribed Angle vs. Central Angle

body.en: A central angle has its vertex at the center of the circle, while an inscribed angle has its vertex on the circle's circumference. The inscribed angle is half the measure of the central angle subtending the same arc. Confusing the two is one of the most common pitfalls on circle questions. Additionally, any inscribed angle that intercepts a diameter (semicircle) is guaranteed to be \( 90^\circ \) (Thales' theorem).

Problem (Medium): In a circle, chords \( XZ \) and \( YD \) intersect at \( P \), with \( PX = 10 \), \( PZ = 32 \), and \( PY = 20 \). Determine the chord segment length \( u = PD \).

Step-by-Step Solution: By the Intersecting Chords Theorem, \( 10 \times 32 = 20 \cdot PD \implies PD = 16 \).

Problem (Hard): A right circular cylinder \( X \) has radius \( r = 6 \), height \( h = 3 \), and volume \( V = h\pi \). Determine the volume factor \( h(u) \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Using \( V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (6^2)(3) = 108\pi \), we get \( h = 108 \).

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Circles)

rows.en: Reading radius of \((x-5)^2 + (y+4)^2 = 16\) as \(r = 16\) or center as \((-5, 4)\)
Confuses \(r^2\) with \(r\) and forgets to flip the signs inside \((x-h)\) and \((y-k)\).
Take the square root and negate the constants: center \((5, -4)\), radius \(r = \sqrt{16} = 4\).
Using SSA (two sides and a non-included angle) to claim triangle congruence
The ambiguous case of the Sine Rule allows two distinct triangles (\(\theta\) and \(180^\circ - \theta\)).
Use valid congruence criteria only: SSS, SAS (included angle), ASA, AAS, or HL/RHS.
Cubing the area ratio \((A_1/A_2)^3\) to find the volume ratio of similar solids
Area ratio is already \(k^2\), so cubing it gives \(k^6\) instead of \(k^3\).
First take the square root to get linear scale factor \(k = \sqrt{A_1/A_2}\), then cube \(k^3\).

body.en: Geometric Auxiliary-Line Strategy (Honors Euclidean & Analytic Geometry): Whenever a circle problem includes a tangent line, draw the radius to the point of tangency and mark \(90^\circ\) immediately; whenever it includes a chord, drop the perpendicular bisector from the center to form a right triangle.

question.en: Points \( A, B, C \) lie on a circle with center \( O \). Inscribed angle \( \angle ABC \) intercepts minor arc \( AC \) and has measure \( 38^{\circ} \). What is the measure of the central angle \( \angle AOC \) intercepting the same arc?

solution.en:
Solution: The measure of a central angle is twice the measure of an inscribed angle that intercepts the same arc:

\[ m\angle AOC = 2 \times m\angle ABC = 2 \times 38^{\circ} = 76^{\circ}. \]

The central angle \( \angle AOC \) has measure \( 76^{\circ} \), and the measure of minor arc \( AC \) is also \( 76^{\circ} \).

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Circles and start from \( A, B, C \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( m\angle AOC = 2 \times m\angle ABC = 2 \times 38^{\circ} = 76^{\circ}. \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en: From an external point \(P\), two tangents \(PA\) and \(PB\) are drawn to a circle with radius \(r = 5\ \text{cm}\). The distance from \(P\) to the center of the circle \(O\) is \(13\ \text{cm}\). Find the length of the tangents \(PA\) and \(PB\), and find the perimeter of quadrilateral \(PAOB\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Recognize tangent-radius perpendicularity: Tangents are perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so \(\angle PAO = \angle PBO = 90^{\circ}\). \(\triangle PAO\) is a right triangle with hypotenuse \(PO = 13\) and leg \(OA = 5\).

Step 2: Solve for tangent length using the Pythagorean theorem:

\[ PA = \sqrt{PO^2 - OA^2} = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = \sqrt{144} = 12\text{ cm}. \]

By equal tangent lengths from an external point, \(PB = PA = 12\text{ cm}\).

Step 3: Compute the perimeter of \(PAOB\):

\[ \text{Perimeter} = PA + PB + OA + OB = 12 + 12 + 5 + 5 = 34\text{ cm}. \]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Circles and start from \(P\).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(\angle PAO = \angle PBO = 90^{\circ}\).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en: [Practice 3 · Easy] In \( \triangle XYZ \), midsegment \( DE \) is parallel to base \( YZ \) with \( XD = DY = 24 \) and \( DE = 8 \). Determine the base length \( u = YZ \).

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Circles and start from \( \triangle XYZ \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( YZ = 2 \times DE = 2(8) = 16 \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: By the Midsegment Theorem, \( YZ = 2 \times DE = 2(8) = 16 \).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] A convex octagon \( h_{8} \) has \( n = 8 \) sides. Determine the interior angle sum \( u = (8 - 2) \times 180 \).

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Circles and start from \( h_{8} \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( (8 - 2) \times 180^\circ = 1080^\circ \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: The sum of interior angles is \( (8 - 2) \times 180^\circ = 1080^\circ \).

question.en: [Practice 5 · Hard] In right triangle \( \triangle KLM \), the two perpendicular legs have lengths \( 12 \) and \( 35 \). Determine the perimeter \( u(s) \) of \( \triangle KLM \).

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Circles and start from \( \triangle KLM \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( \sqrt{12^2 + 35^2} = 37 \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: By the Pythagorean theorem, the hypotenuse is \( \sqrt{12^2 + 35^2} = 37 \). The perimeter is \( 12 + 35 + 37 = 84 \).
